observations: body L1-L2: the remark holds for the sinus longissimus, 2R − cos ε, which always exceeds R; the sinus crescens, 2R − cos δ′, equals R when δ′ = 0 and exceeds it otherwise.
body L5, L11, L14, L16, L23: the dashes of «al–Battānī» are long dashes (5.4 to 5.5 pt).

body L5-L9: the remark is right: the latitude and longitude follow from the right ascension and the declination as the altitude and azimuth from the declination and the hour angle, the pole of the ecliptic standing for the zenith at the distance ε from the pole of the equator, that is, for the latitude 90° − ε.
body L9: the minus sign is printed as a long dash (10.2 pt); it is set as a minus sign.
body L12: Nallino's addenda et emendanda (Part I, p. LXXIII) read «199,12, adde: ut cap. XXXIX, p. 78–79.»; the printed line is kept.
body L18: the dash before Schiaparelli's name measures 9.8 pt; the heavy bracket closes his addition, begun on p. 198.
body L19: in the head, the dash after «b)» measures 10.4 pt and the dash of «21–25» 5.5 pt; transcribed as a dash and a long dash.

body L22, L26-L27: rules (α) and (β) are right: AC is the arc, and on the circle of latitude AH = β and HC = β′, so that β = AC − β′ when H lies between A and C (β′ smaller than the arc), and β = β′ − AC when A lies between H and C.
body L26: the minus signs are printed as long dashes (10.2 pt); they are set as minus signs.

body L29-L36: the figure stands at the left of lines 29 to 36, which are set beside it in a narrow measure. It is redrawn from measurements of the print: the meridian QPEDP′, printed a little wider than high, as an ellipse; the equator, from the left of the meridian through the first point of Aries to D, and the ecliptic, to E, as straight lines; the axes PP′ and QQ′ in dashes, each dash where it printed; the circle of declination PAB, to P′, and the circle of latitude QACQ′ as arcs; the braces ε (Q to P, between the left ends of the equator and the ecliptic, and E to D), β (A to H), β′ (H to C), 90° − β′ (C to Q′) and 90° − ε (D to Q′), with their labels, the last two turned along the curves; the bold italic letters, the sign of Aries and the italic words aequator and ecliptica.
body L29-L34: the letters of the figure named in the text are upright, in the type of the text; in the formulas they are italic.

body L33-L37: the derivation is right: in the triangle ABC, right-angled at B, sin AB = sin AC sin C; in the triangle CDQ′, right-angled at D, where the meridian meets the equator, sin DQ′ = sin CQ′ sin C, with DQ′ = 90° − ε and CQ′ = 90° − β′, the arcs marked in the figure; hence sin AC = sin δ cos β′/cos ε.
body L39: a short bar, a speck, stands under the a of «arcus».
source_authority: Controlling master page image. Embedded text is not the authority for a reading.
transcription_convention: Source line breaks, hyphenation, quotation signs and word-level type distinctions retained. L numbers count text-bearing lines.
review_responsibility: Transcribed by Claude from the page images; Greek, Arabic, numbers and signs read on enlarged images. Not reviewed by a person.
